findings.summary: Holding an armed PR does not stop GitHub auto-merge. `prHold` only adds the label and posts a comment. Only `runMergeIfEligible` turns auto-merge off, and only when something runs it again on the PR. The reconciler never does: `decide()` returns `held` before every other branch, `held` is exempt from execution, and the reconciler contains no disarm call. Failure scenario: an executor delivers arcana-website #184 and arms it while checks are pending, which is the normal delivered state. The planner then runs `cli-hierarchy pr-hold 184 --reason ...`. Each tick, the reconciler records `held` and takes no action. When the required checks go green, GitHub merges the PR, which is the failure this task was meant to prevent. Fix: have `prHold` run `gh pr merge <n> --disable-auto` (allow it to fail when the PR is not armed). Better still, also have the reconciler disarm a PR that is held and armed. Add a test for each.

findings.summary: The hold check runs before the trust checks, so the gate turns off auto-merge on any armed PR with the label, untrusted ones included. This is safe because it only tightens: removing auto-merge cannot make anything merge. Adding a label needs GitHub triage or write access, so a fork author or outside author cannot put the label on to trigger a disarm. Anyone with write access can remove the label by hand, which ends the hold. That is a usability property, not a weakness, because the label exists only to tighten. No change required.

findings.summary: Every non-zero exit from `gh pr merge --disable-auto` is read as 'the PR was not armed'. A real failure, such as a network or permission error on a PR that is armed, still returns ok with disarmed: false, so the operator may think the hold is complete. The reconciler's `disarm-held` action fixes this on its next pass, so it is not a correctness bug. Still, a warning could be shown on stderr when the gh error text is not the usual 'not enabled' message, or the snapshot could be read to check whether the PR is armed.
